answer: Require hardware-rooted identity: each agent onboards with a TPM/TEE attestation key bound to one physical device, registered once on-ledger. A sybil attacker needs a separate machine per fake identity (~$50+ each), so cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Like a prism splitting light, attestation fingerprints expose mirror-copy fakes — identical software fails the check. New registrations sit in a public per-epoch-capped queue open to peer challenges, so minting a fake is like cracking a walnut: slow, costly, never worth doing in bulk.
